name: apfs_inventory
description: Inventory an APFS container with libfsapfs's fsapfsinfo and say plainly what that reader does not give. path is a container image (a regular file; a link, a directory or a device is refused), offset the byte offset of the container in a disk image (fsapfsinfo -o). The tool runs `fsapfsinfo -V` first and puts its version line in every answer (reader), then fsapfsinfo on the image, in this tool's own process group under the shared process block (a deadline, SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP end the program and what it started; PR_SET_PDEATHSIG on Linux; never a session of its own), reads its output in pieces and writes stdout and stderr, whole, to files (mode 0600, under $OUT/tool-output in a job or work/<your id>/tool-output) that the answer names (stdout_file, stderr_file; a rerun that would replace a larger earlier file writes a new name and says which it kept). Only the first 16 MiB of stdout is read for sections; a program that floods its output is ended at max_output_bytes (default 268435456, stdout and stderr together) and the answer says so; nothing it printed is cut from the files. The output is read as sections (a line that ends in a colon and starts with Container or Volume opens one) of `label : value` lines, and the container section and each volume section are shown with their lines under the reader's own labels, with the labels that look like an identifier, a name, a count (`number of ...`) or an encryption, lock, Fusion or T2 state also named in identifier, name, counts and encryption. Which labels a given build of fsapfsinfo prints is NOT established here: no label is assumed to be present, one that is not there is not reported, and a line that does not parse as a label and value or a heading is counted (unparsed_lines) and makes the answer partial; a number of volumes the reader states that differs from the number of volume sections found, or an output that does not state one, makes it partial. NOT provided, and said in every answer: no snapshot is enumerated and no snapshot content is read (libfsapfs does not support snapshots, Fusion drives or T2 encryption; no snapshot coverage is claimed), no object is extracted (the base pack's icat_extract does not preserve extended attributes either), the view is the container as fsapfsinfo reads it at the offset given, and an encrypted volume is not opened: fsapfsinfo reads a password only from its command line (-p, -r), where the trace records it, so the tool passes none and takes no unlock material. If a volume is reported encrypted, the encrypted-containers pack's volumes/filevault-apfs leaf, when that pack is loaded, covers the unlock route; nothing here shows that a volume is unlocked. A missing fsapfsinfo (it is an optional program of the base pack), a non-zero exit, a deadline, a cap, an output with no Container section, or a refused write to the output directory (a fact about that directory, never about the container) is a failed or partial answer with the reason, never an empty inventory; status is complete only when fsapfsinfo exited 0, its output held a container section and as many volume sections as it states, and nothing is listed under problems. A process fsapfsinfo leaves behind after it exits (a child that holds a descriptor of the kept stdout or stderr file, in a session of its own or not) is stopped, killed and reaped by the shared process block's settle() before the files are kept and counted; one found, or a host where the absence of one cannot be proven (not Linux, PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER refused), makes the answer at most partial (program_group.left_behind, program_group.unproven and a line under problems). A program that ended while something it started held its pipes does not hold the tool (the pipes are let go after one second and what held them, if it is the tool's own, is ended). Volume names and identifiers come from the evidence and pass the shared boundary by their field kind (a value that looks like a token is withheld as <withheld N characters: reason>); the output files hold the reader's text as it printed it, so a name that matters is read there in a job. The tool has no values mode. It has a clock of its own (max_seconds, default 60, at most 100) below the 120 seconds of the manifest; SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end the tool with one JSON answer (interrupted set, exit 128 plus the signal; status partial when a container section had been read before the stop, failed when nothing had been read yet); a signal in the first tens of milliseconds, before the module has run, ends it with no JSON (stated, not closed). Every answer carries status and status_basis.

path.description: An APFS container image: a regular file (a link is refused)

offset.description: Byte offset of the container inside the file (a partition of a disk image), passed to fsapfsinfo -o (default 0)

max_seconds.description: The program's deadline in seconds (default 60, at most 100): at it fsapfsinfo and what it started are ended and the answer is partial or failed

max_output_bytes.description: Bytes of stdout and stderr together that are kept before the program is ended (default 268435456); everything written before that is in the output files
